questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain what is meant by each of the following terms:

(i) Ecosystem

(ii) Food web

(iii) Trophic level

(iv) Population. *(8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) An **ecosystem** is a **community of living organisms (plants, animals and microorganisms) interacting with one another and with the non-living (abiotic) components of their environment** (soil, water, air, light, temperature) in a particular area. *Example:* a pond, a forest.

(ii) A **food web** is a **network of interconnected food chains** in an ecosystem, showing all the feeding relationships, because most organisms feed on, and are eaten by, more than one kind of organism.

(iii) A **trophic level** is the **position or feeding level of an organism in a food chain**, according to its source of energy: producers (first level), primary consumers (second level), secondary consumers (third level), and so on.

(iv) A **population** is a **group of organisms of the same species living together in the same area at the same time**. *Example:* all the tilapia fish in a lake.

questions.enonce_markdown: Describe how energy flows through and is lost from an ecosystem. *(8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Flow of energy**

* The **sun** is the source of energy. **Green plants (producers)** trap light energy by photosynthesis and convert it into **chemical energy** stored in organic food (only about 1 % of the sunlight reaching the plants is trapped).
* This energy passes along the food chain as organisms are eaten: from the producers to the **primary consumers (herbivores)**, then to the **secondary and tertiary consumers (carnivores)**.
* When plants and animals die, the energy remaining in their bodies goes to the **decomposers** (bacteria and fungi), which feed on the dead matter and wastes.
* Energy flows **in one direction only** (it is not recycled) and **decreases at each trophic level**.

**Loss of energy** (so only about 10 % passes to the next trophic level)

1. **Respiration**: much of the energy is used by each organism for life processes and is **lost as heat** to the surroundings.
2. **Movement and other activities** use energy, which is released as heat.
3. **Part of the food is not eaten** (roots, bones, fur, wood) or is **not digested and is lost in faeces and urine** (excretory wastes).
4. **Parts of organisms die** and are not eaten by the next level (they pass to the decomposers).
5. Heat is lost to the surroundings, for example in maintaining the body temperature of birds and mammals.

Eventually all the energy is **lost as heat** to the environment.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Construct a food chain with four trophic levels from the following list of organisms: hawk, small birds, garden snails, lettuce and man.

(ii) Explain why most food chains consist of not more than four or at most five trophic levels? *(4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A food chain with four trophic levels:

$$\text{lettuce} \longrightarrow \text{garden snails} \longrightarrow \text{small birds} \longrightarrow \text{hawk}$$

(lettuce = producer, 1st trophic level; garden snails = primary consumer; small birds = secondary consumer; hawk = tertiary consumer, the top carnivore). The arrows show the direction of energy flow. (An equally acceptable chain with man at the top is: lettuce $\rightarrow$ garden snails $\rightarrow$ small birds $\rightarrow$ man.)

(ii) Food chains are short because **energy is lost at each trophic level**: only about **10 %** of the energy is passed on to the next level, since the rest is lost as **heat in respiration**, in movement, and in **uneaten and undigested parts and wastes**. After four or five levels, **the energy left is too little to support another population of organisms** (the number and the biomass of organisms also decrease).
